answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on misbehavior, like a canyon toll: every crossing costs, so flooding the network with fake identities means paying the toll thousands of times. A lightweight verification check, as cheap as a zephyr breeze for one honest agent, becomes a heavy burden when an attacker must pass it for every sock puppet. Each identity reputation is also a single thread that cannot be copied or transferred, so fresh identities start with zero trust and cannot inherit a good history.
